title: Exact free induction and the cyclic resolution in ordinary derived categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and let $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be an exact autoequivalence, with chosen inverse and coherent integer powers. Let $\mathcal W=\mathcal A^P$ be the category of pairs $(M,\phi:PM\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ and intertwining morphisms [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and small coproducts in one fixed indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Then $\mathcal W$ is Grothendieck abelian. The functor $U:\mathcal W\to\mathcal A$ forgetting $\phi$ is exact, conservative, and preserves coproducts. The free functor $I:\mathcal A\to\mathcal W$ has underlying object
$$UI(M)=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}P^nM,$$
with structure $P(UI(M))\xrightarrow{\sim}UI(M)$ reindexing the summand $P(P^nM)$ to the summand numbered $n+1$. It is exact and left adjoint to $U$. Termwise application gives an exact adjunction $I:D(\mathcal A)\rightleftarrows D(\mathcal W):U$, with $U$ conservative and preserving coproducts.

For a complex $K$ in $\mathcal W$, write $\phi:P(UK)\xrightarrow{\sim}UK$ for its chain isomorphism and $\phi_n:P^nUK\xrightarrow{\sim}UK$ for its iterates, including negative powers. There is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes in $\mathcal W$
$$0\longrightarrow IUK\xrightarrow{d_K}IUK\xrightarrow{\epsilon_K}K\longrightarrow0,$$
where $\epsilon_K$ on the underlying summand numbered $n$ is $\phi_n$, and
$$U(d_K)\iota_n=\iota_n-\iota_{n-1}\,P^{n-1}(\phi).$$
The counit is $\epsilon_K$. It induces a distinguished triangle $IUK\to IUK\to K\to IUK[1]$ in $D(\mathcal W)$, natural in the derived object $K$. In particular an object with underlying complex in a localizing subcategory $\mathcal L\subset D(\mathcal A)$ belongs to the localizing subcategory generated by $I(\mathcal L)$ in $D(\mathcal W)$. Here localizing means full, closed under isomorphisms, shifts, distinguished cones and small coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

proof.text: For a family $(M_a,\phi_a)$, put $V=\bigoplus_aM_a$ in $\mathcal A$. The equivalence $P$ preserves this coproduct by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], so $PV\cong\bigoplus_aPM_a\xrightarrow{\oplus\phi_a}V$ is an isomorphism. This makes $V$ a fixed pair. A morphism $V\to N$ intertwines its structure with that of $N$ precisely when its restriction to every summand does: check the equation after $P$ of each coprojection, which jointly determine a map out of $PV$. Thus this is the coproduct in $\mathcal W$ and $U$ preserves it, including the empty family.

Use the specified localization construction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] on Free.adjunction, preserving its actual termwise unit and counit. For conservativity of D(U), a morphism whose image is invertible induces invertible underlying homology maps: use the exact-functor homology comparison, then reflect these isomorphisms through U. The derived homology criterion makes the original morphism invertible.

proof.text: Both hearts are Grothendieck by step 1, so the existing K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] apply in each. Step 2 gives coproduct preservation by the exact forgetful functor. Apply [lem-pur-exact-derived-coproducts], the proved general theorem that an exact coproduct-preserving functor induces a coproduct-preserving functor on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Its arbitrary indexing universe specializes to the fixed universe w.

For a complex $K$ of fixed pairs, put $M=UK$. Its structure $\phi:PM\to M$ is a chain isomorphism. Coherent iteration, in both directions, gives chain isomorphisms $\phi_n:P^nM\to M$ with $\phi_0=1$ and
$$\phi_{n+1}=\phi\,P(\phi_n)=\phi_nP^n(\phi).$$
The map $\epsilon_K:I(M)\to K$ whose underlying restriction to summand $n$ is $\phi_n$ intertwines structures by the first equality: on $P(P^nM)$ the two sides are $\phi P(\phi_n)$ and $\phi_{n+1}$. Under the free adjunction it restricts on summand zero to $1_M$, hence is the counit. These are chain maps and are natural in $K$, since a fixed-pair chain map $f$ satisfies $Uf\,\phi_n=\phi'_nP^n(Uf)$ by positive and negative iteration of its intertwining equation.

proof.text:
Define a chain endomorphism $s_K$ of $I(M)$ on underlying summands by
$$Us_K\,\iota_n=\iota_{n-1}P^{n-1}(\phi).$$
It intertwines the free successor structure: applying $P$ to the displayed summand map and then the successor structure gives $\iota_nP^n(\phi)$, as does applying the successor structure first and then $s_K$ on summand $n+1$. This uses only the coherent identifications $P(P^nM)\cong P^{n+1}M$. Thus $d_K=1-s_K$ is a morphism of complexes in $\mathcal W$ with exactly the asserted formula. The second equality of step 5 gives $U\epsilon_K\,Us_K\,\iota_n=\phi_{n-1}P^{n-1}(\phi)=\phi_n$, so $\epsilon_Kd_K=0$ by faithfulness of $U$. The same summand formula and $Uf\,\phi=\phi'P(Uf)$ show $I(Uf)d_K=d_{K'}I(Uf)$.

proof.text:
Identify $UI(M)$ with $S=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M$ by the chain isomorphism sending summand $P^nM$ via $\phi_n$ to summand $M$. With coprojections $e_n:M\to S$, the two underlying maps become $D e_n=e_n-e_{n-1}$ and $a e_n=1_M$. Define $h:S\to S$ by
$$he_n=\begin{cases}\sum_{j=1}^n e_j&n>0,\\0&n=0,\\-\sum_{j=n+1}^0 e_j&n<0.\end{cases}$$
Each column is a finite sum of chain maps, so the coproduct universal property defines $h$ on the entire complex, with no support assumption on maps into a coproduct. Telescoping gives $Dhe_n=e_n-e_0$, $hDe_n=e_n$ and $ae_0=1$ for every $n$, including $n=0,-1$. Hence $Dh=1-e_0a$ and $hD=1$. In each degree $D$ is monic, $a$ is split epic, and for every $x:T\to S$ with $ax=0$ one has $x=Dhx$, uniquely since $hD=1$. Therefore $D$ is the kernel of $a$ and the underlying sequence is degreewise short exact.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact] to the singleton family consisting of $U:\mathcal W\to\mathcal A$, degree by degree. It preserves zero morphisms and finite limits and colimits because it is additive exact, and reflects isomorphisms by step 1. Step 6 gives the zero composite; step 7 gives underlying short exactness. The result is precisely the asserted degreewise short exact sequence in $\mathcal W$. No splitting in $\mathcal W$ is claimed or needed.

source.place: JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.shortExact_iff, singleton family; source of the cited existing Mathlib leaf

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] in the abelian category $\mathcal W$ to step 8. It gives the distinguished triangle
$$IUK\xrightarrow{d_K}IUK\xrightarrow{\epsilon_K}K\xrightarrow{\delta_K}IUK[1],$$
and naturality of $\delta_K$ for every chain map $f:K\to K'$, since steps 5-6 give a morphism of the short exact sequences. Thus $\delta$ is a natural transformation from the cochain localization functor to its composite with $IU[1]$. Both functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by step 3. By the localization property of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this transformation descends to $D(\mathcal W)$: its naturality equation for a quasi-isomorphism also implies the equation for its inverse, and hence for any composition of chain maps and inverses representing a derived morphism. The same holds for $d$ and $\epsilon$. This proves naturality in the derived object, without choosing cones on arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor and lemma-derived-compare-triangles-ses; descent by ordinary localization

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Loc}(I(\mathcal L))$ in $D(\mathcal W)$, with the closure operations specified in the statement and [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. If $UK\in\mathcal L$, then $IUK\in I(\mathcal L)\subset\mathcal C$. Both first vertices of the distinguished triangle of step 9 are therefore in $\mathcal C$. Closure under distinguished cones and isomorphisms gives $K\in\mathcal C$. This argument needs no invariance of $\mathcal L$ under $P$.
